name: Question 3
problem: Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through $P(-1,-4,5)$ and parallel to $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $P$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=p+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

In our case, the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through P(−1,−4,5) and parallel to v=[10−1].

a
r=[10−1]+t[−1−45],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[−1−45]+t[10−1],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[1−10]+t[5−4−1],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[−1−45]+[1−10]
e
r=[−1−45]+t[1−10],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The vector equation of the straight line passing through P and parallel to v is given by r=p+tv,

where t∈(−∞,∞) and p is the position vector of P.

In our case, the position vector of the point P is p=[−1−45].

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

r=[−1−45]+t[10−1],t∈(−∞,∞).
